procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
One year out from MI/PCI (1/2019). Routine f/u.

S: Says he's been good about the pills - uses a weekly pill box now. No chest pain or pressure. No SOB beyond his usual on stairs; denies any change. No palpitations, no swelling.
He asked again about the rheumatic fever - wanted to know if he needs antibiotics before dental work. Reviewed: rheumatic fever as a child, no murmur on any exam here, no valve disease known. No prophylaxis indicated without valve disease. He was relieved.
Smoking: still 1 ppd. The 'stuck inside in winter' quit plan didn't happen.

O: BP 132/84, HR 68. Heart regular, S1 S2 normal, no murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs: decreased air entry, prolonged expiration, no wheeze. Abd soft. Ext no edema.
Fasting lipids drawn this AM.

A/P
1. CAD s/p MI with PCI 1/2019 - doing well, no angina. ASA 81, metoprolol succ 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril.
2. HTN - 132/84, fine.
3. HLD - lipids today.
4. Hx rheumatic fever - no valve disease, no endocarditis prophylaxis needed.
5. COPD - stable, olodaterol daily.
6. Tobacco - 45 pk-yr. Counseled. Declines quit date.
7. AAA - vascular surgery surveillance scan due this spring.

RTC 6 mo for annual wellness.

documents.title: Cholesterol results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lyle - cholesterol panel from Tuesday: LDL 70, HDL 45, triglycerides 150, total 180. LDL is at goal on atorvastatin. The non-HDL number on the report reads 135, a little over the 130 we aim for, because the total came back higher than the other three would add up to. Nothing to change for that; we'll see it again with your wellness labs. -PCP

documents.title: Vascular Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
VASCULAR SURGERY ASSOCIATES
Clinic visit 04/22/2020

Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Haskins on 04/22/2020 for routine surveillance of his abdominal aortic aneurysm.

He has no new complaints. He mentions occasional mild abdominal discomfort, which he puts down to indigestion; nothing in the back, no syncope, nothing he would call pain. He is a current smoker with roughly 40 pack-years.

BP 142/88, heart rate 78.
Abdomen soft. A pulsatile mass is palpable in the periumbilical region, nontender. No abdominal bruit. Peripheral pulses intact.

Labs: hemoglobin 14.2, hematocrit 42%, fasting glucose 98.

Ultrasound that day showed an infrarenal AAA of 4.2 cm.

Impression: Infrarenal AAA, 4.2 cm, below the threshold for repair. His occasional abdominal discomfort does not sound aneurysm-related, but I have asked him to come straight to an emergency department for severe abdominal or back pain.

Plan: repeat ultrasound in 12 months. Continue aspirin and statin. I stressed that smoking is the main modifiable factor in aneurysm growth.

Thank you for allowing me to share in his care.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit (audio only)
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Audio-only visit, pt at home, consented. Pandemic - office doing phone visits for stable chronic f/u.

Vascular surgery letter from 4/22 reviewed with him: AAA 4.2 cm, recheck in a year. He understands to go to the ED for sudden severe belly or back pain. The 'indigestion' comes and goes, no relation to meals he can tell, not worse. No melena, no vomiting.
No chest pain. Breathing same. Staying home mostly. No fever, no cough beyond baseline.
No home BP cuff. Meds filled by mail-order now.
Still smoking.

A/P
- AAA 4.2 cm: surveillance per vascular surgery.
- CAD/HTN/HLD: continue meds.
- COPD: stable.
- Tobacco: counseled by phone. No date.
- Mild intermittent abdominal discomfort: vascular surgeon not concerned; he'll tell me if it changes.

AWV in July, in person if office allows.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT (initial)

No complaints today. Adherent to meds (pill box). Vascular surgery saw him in April - AAA 4.2 cm, annual scans.

Health risk assessment: lives independently, drives, manages his own meds and money. No falls in the past year, no fear of falling, gets up from the chair without his hands. Hearing ok in quiet rooms. Vision - readers only.
PHQ-2: 0. AUDIT-C: 2.
Tobacco: 1 ppd, now 45 pack-years. Not ready to quit.

Vitals: BP 132/84, HR 70, SpO2 94% RA.
Exam: Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs diminished bilaterally with prolonged expiration. Abd soft, pulsatile midline mass, nontender. Ext no edema, pedal pulses palpable.

Prevention review: Going back through his chart and the old records, he has had no cancer screening of any kind in at least five years - no colonoscopy or stool test ever, no lung screening despite qualifying for years. Should have been addressed earlier. Talked through both today:
- Lung: he meets criteria (age 66, current smoker, 45 pk-yr). Shared decision-making done - benefits, false positives, radiation, the chance of follow-up scans. He agrees to annual low-dose CT. Ordered.
- Colon: he refuses colonoscopy ('not putting myself through that'). Agrees to a yearly FIT. Kit given.
- Immunizations: Tdap 2018, PPSV23 2019, flu yearly. Shingrix - will check pharmacy coverage again.
- Hep C screen done 2018, negative.

Labs today: BMP, CBC, lipids.

A/P
1. AWV - personalized prevention plan given in writing.
2. Lung cancer screening - LDCT ordered.
3. Colorectal screening - FIT.
4. Chronic: HTN at goal, CAD stable, COPD stable, AAA under surveillance - no med changes.
5. Tobacco - counseled, declined.

RTC 4 mo.

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Roomed for AWV. Mask on. HRA questionnaire completed with pt. Med list reviewed, no changes. FIT kit given with instructions.

documents.title: Result call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt with AWV labs per PCP: hemoglobin 14.2, fasting sugar 98, creatinine 1.0 - all fine. Cholesterol stable on atorvastatin. Radiology will call to schedule his lung CT. Reminded him to mail the FIT kit.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING - BASELINE
Clinical: 66M, current smoker, 45 pack-years.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast.
Comparison: None.
Lungs: Centrilobular emphysema, upper lobe predominant. 4 mm solid nodule in the right upper lobe (series 3, image 61). No other nodules. No consolidation.
Pleura: No effusion or pneumothorax.
Mediastinum: No lymphadenopathy.
Upper abdomen: Unremarkable within the limited field.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 2: benign appearance or behavior. 4 mm right upper lobe solid nodule. Centrilobular emphysema. Recommend continued annual screening with LDCT in 12 months.

documents.title: LDCT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt myself re lung screening CT: Lung-RADS 2. One tiny 4 mm nodule, benign category, nothing to do except the routine yearly CT next August. Scan also shows emphysema, which fits his COPD. Used it as another push on smoking - he listened, no commitment.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Repeat in 1 year. Portal message sent.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u CAD, HTN, COPD, AAA.

No angina. Breathing about the same; more cough in the cold mornings, white. No fevers. Isolating at home a lot, which he says means more cigarettes, not fewer.
All meds by mail-order, no gaps.

BP 126/86, HR 77, SpO2 94%.
Exam: masked. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs distant, prolonged exp, few end-exp wheezes. Abd soft. Ext no edema; DP palpable both sides.

A/P
1. CAD s/p MI - stable, continue regimen.
2. HTN - 126/86, acceptable.
3. COPD/emphysema - stable on olodaterol.
4. Tobacco - pandemic made it worse. Counseled. Declines quit date; would consider patches 'later.'
5. AAA 4.2 cm - next scan spring.
6. HM - LDCT Lung-RADS 2 (next 8/2021), FIT neg 8/2020, flu done.

RTC 3 mo.
